transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

Hi, Doc. Well, I guess what brings me in is that I'm having a lot of trouble staying focused at work. I'm a construction manager, and... like, I can sit down to start a safety briefing or a plan review, and I'll be trying really hard to pay attention. But within just a few minutes, my mind is already off on three other job problems. 

Because of that, I keep missing things in the plans or the meetings that I know I should have caught. It's getting pretty bad, so I figured I needed to come in and talk to somebody about it.
Did you have similar trouble focusing or staying organized when you were a child?

Yeah, I did. Actually, back in, uh, elementary school, my teachers were already telling my parents about it. They said I just couldn't stay in my seat and that I was always talking out of turn. 

And as far as staying organized... I lost my homework all the time. Whenever they gave us directions for an assignment, I'd just rush right through them before I really even understood what I was supposed to be doing. So, yeah, it's definitely been going on since I was a kid.
How has your mood been lately?

My mood? Uh, it's been fine, mostly. I mean, I get frustrated with myself when I mess up at work, but overall, I wouldn't say I'm feeling down or depressed or anything like that. Just... stressed about the mistakes, you know?
Do you often feel nervous or worried most days?

No, not really. I mean, I worry about getting fired if I keep screwing up the blueprints or missing things in the briefings, but I wouldn't say I'm an anxious person in general. It's just the work stuff that gets to me.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has a longstanding pattern of inattention and hyperactivity/impulsivity beginning in childhood, now causing clear work-related impairment. Symptoms include distractibility, missing details, disorganization, losing homework, difficulty staying seated as a child, and talking out of turn. No evidence was provided for a mood, anxiety, or trauma-related disorder.
